---
applyTo: "packages/genui/server/service/{a2ui,openui,lynx-xml,html}/*bench*.ts,packages/genui/server/service/common/bench/**,packages/genui/server/app/a2ui/bench/**,packages/genui/playground/src/pages/bench/**,packages/genui/server/rslib.config.ts"
---

Bench generation must inherit `reasoningEffort` from each group's selected server model for every protocol and repair attempt. Do not suppress the setting through `inheritReasoningEffort: false`; unconfigured models retain their upstream defaults.

Use `service/common/bench/retry.ts` for A2UI, OpenUI, Lynx XML, and HTML protocol-adapter transport retries. Keep transport failures and validation repairs in one bounded attempt budget, and explicitly pass `maxRetries: 0` to disable nested SDK retries. Retry only transient HTTP/network failures; stop on cancellation, permanent HTTP errors, and unknown/configuration errors. Honor `Retry-After` seconds and HTTP dates; if the requested wait exceeds the 60-second per-wait budget, stop instead of retrying early. Otherwise use bounded exponential backoff starting at one second. Keep waits abortable, do not add transport failures to repair prompts, and preserve known failed-attempt usage. Only sanitized numeric retry decisions may enter artifacts, never raw provider exceptions or headers. Verify actual upstream call counts with real Mastra and deterministic HTTP mocks for both Chat Completions and Responses APIs.

A2UI bench jobs run agent generation and validation in `genui-server`, but browser-backed render metrics remain disabled. Keep browser metrics marked as disabled in reports.

Make the compact Bench progress footer expandable into an independently scrolling workflow, grouped by comparison group with a stable row for every scenario and repeat. Track generation (including validation, repairs, and XML conversion), browser screenshot/upload, and model scoring separately; distinguish future stages, queue waits, execution, failure, skipping, and cancellation. Emit screenshot and scoring phases at actual admission boundaries, retain every run's latest state in snapshots and reports, and use per-run revisions so SSE replay cannot rewind the UI. Refresh the snapshot after bounded event replay to restore evicted phases. Preserve completed stages when cancelling and show unrecorded legacy stages as Not recorded instead of inventing a failure location. Keep history disclosures usable when the plan is read-only.

Bench permits at most eight comparison groups, including disabled groups and the baseline. Enforce the same limit in the Playground and server, and reject oversized requests rather than silently truncating groups. Derive generation workers from enabled groups; do not expose or submit Concurrency or include parallelism in BenchSettings or new reports. Ignore legacy request parallelism and omit it when restoring configuration; keep old history readable without displaying the obsolete field.

Record job startedAt at admission and completedAt only after every pipeline stage drains, including failure and cancellation cleanup. Measure durationMs with a monotonic clock across queueing, generation, repairs, XML conversion, browser screenshots, and scoring; freeze it in the terminal report and snapshots. Display elapsed time while running and persist total duration with start/end timestamps in history and reports. Anchor the live timer to the creation response, not replayed SSE events. Older reports lack true start/duration fields: show Not recorded instead of subtracting their createdAt and completedAt, which were both written at report creation.

Pipeline Bench generation separately from browser capture and model scoring. Start one worker per enabled comparison group. Each group generates scenarios in request order and repeats in ascending order; it must finish generation, validation, repairs, and XML conversion for one run before generating the next. Groups run independently, without the former sample-order rotation, and results remain paired by scenario and repeat IDs. Share eight generation slots and two scoring slots across all Bench jobs in the server process; the five scoring dimensions within one evaluation remain parallel. Announce each screenshot-ready artifact through screenshot-requested immediately after generation and validation, without acquiring a server capture slot. The Playground queues capture IDs and runs one capture/upload worker per job; fetch task content only when dequeuing it. That GET acknowledges capture start: begin its execution timeout then, not when the SSE event was sent. Keep the acknowledgement idempotent, preserve pending events across replay, deduplicate queued/active/completed IDs in the browser, and discard queued work on cancellation. Bound a missing-browser admission wait by the in-flight capacity times the per-capture timeout; settling or cancelling a task must also release its start waiter. Reserve a bounded in-flight slot before generation, with capacity equal to group workers plus two scoring slots plus one capture, so slow scoring applies backpressure instead of accumulating artifacts. Keep all queue waits abortable and outside Agent/Judge execution timeouts and metrics; retries must re-enter the same stage limits. Finish all active and queued work before publishing a terminal report or clearing credentials, and drain aborted scoring dimensions before releasing their shared slot. Record Agent time at the end of generation and validation for every protocol, including XML conversion but excluding queue, capture, and scoring time. Keep the single SSE subscription and correlate interleaved results through run and capture IDs.

Lynx XML participates in Bench as `lynx-xml` with the `native` profile and no component catalog. Reuse its existing generation service and document normalization, retain its deterministic fragment conversion, and disable search and image generation. Send the final XML document to the browser as screenshot-task source, outside multipart fields. The Playground packages it as `index.lynxml` in a ZIP and calls `POST /screenshot/zip/upload` with multipart `file`, `entry=index.lynxml`, `width`, and `height`; never send a `source` form field to this route; do not wrap XML in an A2UI/OpenUI bundle or send globalProps, model settings, or model evaluation options. Reuse BMP conversion, GenUI scoring, cancellation, and report storage. Keep XML protocol identity in history and every report label, and preserve the user's baseline protocol when adding comparisons.

Let every comparison group select its model independently, but expose and accept only public model names returned by the GenUI server. Do not add a free-form Bench model input or reinterpret an unknown group model as an upstream model ID.

Preserve exact configured public model names in structured Bench `model` fields even when they equal a private upstream model ID; keep upstream IDs and provider credentials redacted in diagnostics and unrecognized model fields. Preserve generated comparison `id`/`groupId` values through history serialization so reports can join the saved plan. Older redacted group IDs may recover model names only through a unique match on name, protocol, profile, and role in the same history entry; never guess from another group, array order, or the current default model.

Use the Rust HTTP service for Lynx screenshots and deterministic comparison, and GenUI Server for model evaluation. The Playground alone reads its locally configured `UI_JUDGE_SERVER_URL`, probes `/health`, and sends multipart capture requests. GenUI must never contact this address. Instead, issue screenshot tasks to the active browser, accept bounded BMP uploads or capture errors, and convert validated BMP to PNG before scoring with the Bench group's model. Keep bundle URLs server-owned, reject nonempty `judgeSteps` before capture, and preserve sanitization for every protocol.

Cancel an unread screenshot response body before rejecting its media type or advertised content length, so rejected captures release sidecar connections. Await cleanup and tolerate cancellation failures without replacing the validation error. Once a reader has been acquired, keep cancellation and lock release in its existing cleanup path. Cover both early rejection paths with deterministic streams, including cancellation failures and absent bodies.

Treat UI Judge scoring as atomic at the Bench boundary. Any visual-score, GEQI dimension, aggregate-contract, request, or response error must set both the judge and the containing run to failed, force the persisted judge score to zero, omit partial dimension and GEQI aggregates, and exclude the run from Judge averages. Apply this consistently to native A2UI and protocol-adapter A2UI/OpenUI paths; keep screenshots and error messages only as failure diagnostics.

Decode only the runner's top-down 32-bit BITMAPV4HEADER layout with its RGBA masks. Bound input bytes and dimensions before allocation, and preserve alpha during asynchronous PNG compression. Set `mediaType: "image/png"` on Mastra image parts so its message conversion does not default to JPEG. Cover the real provider and structured-output path with deterministic HTTP responses, including local data-URL decoding. Use the full converted PNG for model evaluation; apply the separate per-image and per-job limits only when storing Bench screenshots. Malformed captures fail evaluation. Preserve the visual-correctness score and four GEQI dimensions with weights 30/25/15/15, normalized to 0-100. Reuse the GenUI provider, reasoning settings, output-token ceiling, and cancellation signal; abort sibling evaluations if a dimension fails.

Never let model-generated Bench messages make the server-side headless renderer load resources. Remove `openUrl` from every Bench prompt catalog, replace `Image`, `LazyComponent`, `LineChart`, `McpApp`, and `PieChart` definitions with inert placeholders, downgrade Markdown `Text`, and reject recursive `openUrl` function calls before calling UI Judge. The headless resource callback can otherwise read `file://` paths, access arbitrary HTTP endpoints, load executable nested bundles, or block its single capture worker on an unbounded download.

Do not add `@sparticuz/chromium` or `playwright-core` back to `packages/genui/server`. Keep the entire browser-backed implementation in `a2ui-bench-preview.ts` and its runner import and call sites commented until preview rendering moves to its dedicated service. Do not add a fallback preview implementation, capability flag, or configuration switch while it is disabled.

Bench job event streams can sit in a long-running phase without producing run events. Keep the `/a2ui/bench/jobs/[jobId]/events` SSE response alive with heartbeat comments, and let native EventSource disconnects reconnect unless the server sends an explicit `event: error` payload. Otherwise proxies or serverless hosts may close an idle stream and the playground will lose a still-running job.

Preserve generation usage for every Bench protocol and sum all generation steps and repair attempts, excluding UI Judge calls. Keep missing input, output, cache-read, cache-write, and reasoning counts unknown rather than zero; a partial retry breakdown must not appear complete. Cache counts are subsets of input and reasoning is a subset of output, so never add them to total tokens again. Keep numeric and nested AI SDK usage formats plus snake-case provider formats readable in older browser history, and divide group breakdowns by the same planned-run denominator as avgTokens.

Request a 390 × 844 portrait viewport by default for every protocol. Preserve separate `/screenshot/template` and `/screenshot/lynxml` endpoints, both using multipart fields including width and height. Do not modify `packages/genui/ui-judge` to support browser transport; report missing deployment CORS support explicitly.

Default new A2UI groups and switches from another protocol to A2UI to native with Full Catalog. Adding comparisons must not rewrite existing groups' profiles or catalogs; preserve manual A2UI choices when cloning model/prompt comparisons or retaining the same protocol.

HTML participates in Bench as `html` with the `native` profile and no catalog. Reuse the HTML generation service and document normalizer, preserve usage through repairs, and disable search and image generation. Issue `browser/html` screenshot tasks containing only the complete source and viewport dimensions. HTML-only jobs do not need a UI Judge service URL or sidecar health probe. Invoke `getDisplayMedia` from the Start run user gesture and validate current-tab sharing with Element Capture before creating the server job. Keep HTML in a script-capable sandbox without same-origin access, prepend a restrictive resource CSP, serialize captures on the shared track, and read only fresh restricted video frames. Encode browser pixels in the existing top-down 32-bit BMP transport, retaining server PNG conversion and model scoring. Stop tracks and remove capture frames on cancellation, terminal events, startup failures, and late permission grants. Never introduce a server browser or DOM-to-image substitute. Feature-detect desktop Element Capture and give actionable sharing guidance.

Screen Capture can deliver only one frame for a static HTML page. Register the video-frame callback before starting playback instead of waiting for another frame after `play()`. Keep one video consumer attached to the shared stream between captures: detaching every consumer can suspend Chromium's track and stall the next Element Capture restriction. Verify repeated captures with static inline-script/canvas fixtures, and keep the requested iframe viewport independent of its on-screen fit scale.
